reading.title: A Lost Coin
reading.text: On Friday I get pocket money from Dad. This week I put the coins in my back pocket. On my way to the shop, I noticed there was a hole in the pocket, and one coin was gone! Also, a button came off my coat, and the zip on my bag was stuck. Mum sewed the button on and fixed the hole. Then she gave me another coin. I put it in my front pocket this time.

listening.title: In the Car
listening.script: We were driving to my grandfather's house. Dad said, "Fasten your seat belts, please." My little brother pushed a button and the window opened. It was cold, so I pulled up the zip on my jacket. Dad has a leather belt with a big silver buckle. Grandpa waited at the gate. When we arrived, he put some sweets in my pocket.

reading.title: Packing a Bag
reading.text: On Friday evening I pack my bag for school. First I open my bag and take out the old papers. Then I put in my books, a pencil case and a bottle of water. My school bag is quite heavy, so I carry it on my back. Last week I left my bag at my friend's house. Fortunately, he brought it to school. Now I always check my bag twice.

listening.title: Camping
listening.script: Our class went camping last weekend. Each of us had a sleeping bag and an overnight bag. My bag had a torch, a bag of sweets and a plastic bag for rubbish. The teacher carried the heavy bag with food. At night it was cold, but my sleeping bag was warm. In the morning we picked up all the rubbish and put it in the plastic bag.

reading.title: The Found Wallet
reading.text: Last Saturday I found a leather wallet in the park. It was full of money and it had an ID card inside. I did not take anything. I gave the wallet to my father, and he phoned the owner. The man was very happy. He said he had lost his wallet on the bus. As a thank you, he sent me a card with a drawing of a dog. I put the card on my wall.

listening.title: At the Shop
listening.script: Yesterday Mum and I went to the supermarket. At the till, Mum took out her wallet. The shop assistant said, "Do you pay by card or cash?" Mum paid by credit card. We also bought a birthday card for my cousin and a postcard for me to collect. At home we played cards, and I won twice.

reading.title: Lost Keys
reading.text: This morning I could not find my keys. I looked in my bag and in my pockets. Mum has a big bunch of keys with a key ring in the shape of a star. I only have one front door key. Finally I found it under my bed, next to Grandma's gold ring. I do not know how it got there! I locked the door, and the school bell was already ringing when I arrived.

listening.title: A Birthday Gift
listening.script: For her birthday, Aigul got a small gold ring from her parents. She wears the ring on her finger every day. Her father also gave her a key ring with a tiny house. "This is the key to our new home," he said, and he gave her a key. The phone rang and it was her grandmother. Aigul told her about the ring, and Grandma said, "Give me a ring tomorrow."

reading.title: New Glasses
reading.text: Last month the teacher noticed that I could not read the board. So Mum took me to the eye doctor. I need glasses! I chose a pair with thick black frames. At first I forgot to put them on, but now I wear them all day. Last week I dropped them and broke one side, but Dad fixed them. I clean my glasses every evening with a soft cloth.

listening.title: Contact Lenses
listening.script: My older sister Madina wears contact lenses. Before, she wore glasses with thick lenses, and she was shy. Now she puts in her lenses every morning and feels more confident. She still keeps her old glasses for reading at night. On the beach she wears sunglasses. Once she lost one lens in the sea, and we looked for it for an hour. We never found it.

reading.title: A Rainy Day
reading.text: Yesterday it rained all day, and I forgot to take my umbrella. My friend Jasur put up his folding umbrella, and we walked home under one umbrella. The wind was strong, and it nearly blew inside out. I looked at my watch. It was already five, but my watch was ten minutes slow. At home I watched a film about the sea with my sister.

listening.title: Grandpa's Watch
listening.script: My grandfather has an old gold watch. He wears it every day on his left wrist. He sets it by the church clock each Sunday. When it rains, he always takes his black umbrella and says, "Watch out for puddles!" Last week he left his umbrella at the post office, but a kind lady brought it back. He gave her a big smile.
